flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad — this quarter it was a net BENEFIT of $2,123M: transferring the Apple Card portfolio released $2,480M of reserves, more than covering the quarter's charge-offs, so the line added money back instead of costing money.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and bonuses — Goldman's biggest cost by far, rising with the firm's strong results.

opex.name: Transaction based
opex.note: Costs that rise and fall with trading and deal volume: brokerage, clearing and exchange fees.

opex.name: Communications and technology
opex.note: Trading systems, market data and communications.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of offices, systems and equipment over their useful lives.

opex.name: Occupancy
opex.note: Rent and running costs for offices around the world.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Everything else that does not fit the lines above.

oneTimers: The Apple Card transition is the quarter's big one-timer: -$2,258M in net revenues, -$2,481M in provision for credit losses (a benefit), +$38M in operating expenses — a net +$185M pre-tax, +$145M after tax. Excluding it, revenue was $15.7B and EPS was $13.55.
Preferred stock dividends of $233M sit between net earnings ($4,617M) and the $4,384M applicable to common shareholders.

segments.name: Noninterest revenues
segments.note: Fees and trading: Global Banking & Markets brought in $10.4B and Asset & Wealth Management $4.7B, partly offset by a $1.7B negative contribution from Platform Solutions as the Apple Card portfolio was marked down for transfer.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and investments, minus interest paid — up 58% from a year ago on lower funding costs and more interest-earning assets.

takeaways.text: Global Banking & Markets revenue rose 22% to $10.4B — investment banking fees +25%, equities +25% with record financing, FICC +12% — the engine more than offset the Apple Card markdown.
takeaways.title: Banking & markets had a record quarter

takeaways.text: Agreeing to hand Apple Card to another issuer cut revenue by $2,258M (a markdown on the loan portfolio) but released $2,480M of credit reserves in the provision line — a net $145M boost to net earnings after tax and related costs.
takeaways.title: Apple Card exit cut both ways

takeaways.text: Net earnings rose 12% to $4.6B and diluted EPS rose 17% to $14.01, a 16.0% return on equity — helped by $3.0B of buybacks in the quarter shrinking the share count.
takeaways.title: Profit per share jumped

verdict: Goldman's headline revenue fell 3% to $13.5B only because exiting Apple Card cost a $2.3B markdown — the same exit released $2.5B of loan reserves, and underlying banking and markets revenue was a record, lifting net earnings 12% to $4.6B.
footerNote: Credit-loss provision was a $2,123M benefit — money added back, not spent.
